description: The call graph misses edges, so every consumer of CallGraphComponent and Recursive (activation keying, the transport recursion cut, and fz-kdt.177.9's group solve) treats some recursion as acyclic. Found as the transport-cut hole by the fz-kdt.93 builder (a cycle whose every grounded closure-call edge's target cannot statically reach its owner is uncut) and generalised by the fz-229 refutation (2026-09-16): a function reference mints no edge though a lambda does, and a call through a value contributes no edge even after its targets are resolved. Three commits on fz-kdt.98/call-graph-sees-every-edge, in this order so no census pin is ever raised: fz-kdt.98.2 replaces the component cone walk and the transport reachability walk with one monotone Reaches(f) fact (this also retires the unmemoized statically_reaches walker the fz-kdt.93 refuter flagged); fz-kdt.98.1 folds function references into the construction edge; fz-kdt.98.3 makes the edge fact cumulative over the value-call targets each analysis resolves. Closes when all three land.

comments.text: Generalisation from the fz-229 refutation (2026-09-16): StaticCallees (keying.rs collect_step_edges / collect_tail_edges) emits call-graph edges only for LoweredTail::DirectCall and LoweredStep::Lambda; ClosureCall, Dispatch and FunctionRef emit none, and a protocol callback is a static leaf. So CallGraphComponent under-approximates recursion for every consumer, not only the transport cut: a Settled read gated on component equality deadlocked on three singleton components mutually recursive through &fun/1 values (call/2 applying &pong/1 and &ping/1; reproducer on fz-229). Any consumer that treats out-of-component as acyclic inherits this hole.

title: The call graph misses function-reference and value-call edges, so every consumer of CallGraphComponent and Recursive under-approximates recursion
